name: ReadYou
insteadOf: Google Discover / Feedly / Flipboard / doom-scrolling Twitter for news
hook: A magazine-grade Material You RSS reader that replaces algorithmic feeds with the blogs and news sites you actually follow.
bullets: Subscribe to any RSS/Atom feed or import your whole OPML in one go
Parses full article content into a clean, typography-first reading layout
Feed groups, unread filters, starred articles, and search across everything
Syncs articles in the background and notifies you when new ones land
benefits: Your morning briefing, minus the algorithm deciding what enrages you
Articles load as distraction-free pages that read like a premium magazine
Everything is available offline — synced articles stay on your device
Move subscriptions in and out with OPML; no lock-in, ever
setupSteps: Install ReadYou from F-Droid or the project's GitHub releases
Import an OPML file from your old reader, or add feed URLs one by one
Group feeds into folders like News, Blogs, and Tech
Read in the app — new articles sync in the background
details: ReadYou is a free, open-source RSS reader for Android built around Material You. Instead of letting an algorithm decide what you see, you subscribe to the feeds you actually care about — blogs, news sites, tech journals — by URL or by importing an OPML export from Feedly, Feedbin, or any other reader. It fetches articles on a schedule, notifies you when new ones arrive, and can parse full article content, so even stripped-down feeds show up complete. Reading happens in a clean, typography-focused layout with light and dark themes that follow your wallpaper, and everything you have synced is available offline. Filters for unread and starred items, feed folders, search, and OPML export round it out. The project lives at ReadYouApp/ReadYou on GitHub and is licensed under GPL-3.0.
setup: App (Android) — add feeds or import OPML
